name: Question 3
problem:
Suppose that

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$

are eigenvectors of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=5$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-5,$ respectively. Find the matrix $A.$
worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 3\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 3\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot \frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}(5\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 3\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{10}(5\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 3 & 9\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot [\begin{aligned}9 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}-40 & 30 \\ 30 & 40\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 3 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3

Suppose that

v1=[13] and v2=[−31]

are eigenvectors of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A that correspond to the eigenvalues λ1=5 and λ2=−5, respectively. Find the matrix A.

[−4114]

[−4221]

e

Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The spectral decomposition of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A is given by

A=λ1u1⋅u1T+λ2u2⋅u2T, where u1 and u2 are orthonormal eigenvectors of A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2, respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

u1=v1‖v1‖=110[13]u2=v2‖v2‖=110[−31]

Therefore, we have

A=λ1u1u1T+λ2u2u2T=5⋅110[13]⋅110[13]+(−5)⋅110[−31]⋅110[−31]=5⋅110[13][13]+(−5)⋅110[−31][−31]=110(5⋅[13][13]+(−5)⋅[−31][−31])=110(5⋅[1339]+(−5)⋅[9−3−31])=110[−40303040]=[−4334].
